newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan digs anti-smuggling trench on Iraq border.
newsitem.headline: Jordan digs anti-smuggling trench on Iraq border.

text.p: Jordan is digging a trench on its desert border with Iraq as part of a campaign to clamp down on widespread smuggling, Interior Minister Nazir Rasheed said in remarks published on Saturday.

"They are currently digging a trench across the Iraqi- Jordanian border at a length of 170 km (106 miles) and three metres (10 feet) wide and four metres (13 feet) deep," he said of efforts by the armed forces to clamp down on smuggling of drugs and other contraband.
Rasheed was quoted as telling the daily al-Rai newspaper that nearly 60 km (37 miles) had been dug, adding there were plans for a similar trench on the border with Syria.
Jordanian officials say smuggling has been on the rise in recent years and smugglers use the latest high-tech gear to avoid arrest.
"In reality what bothers me is smuggling...Jordan has become a crossroads for smuggling to neighbouring countries because we are in a central location," the minister said.
Officials say international drug gangs smuggle large quantities for neighbouring markets through Jordan. Officials have allocated extra funds for policing the border.
Security forces say there are daily border clashes with infiltrators of mixed nationalities.
"We have begun combating smuggling very severely...and there are tough measures on the border," Rasheed said.
